title: When one source is enough to answer
note: Read by code (src/settling.py) to decide when a needed fact is established and the run can answer at once. A claim from a strong source settles its fact on its own; a claim from any other source needs claims from at least `others_need_sites` independent sites (copies of one document count once). Every claim still needs its word-for-word quote, exact address and the code checks; further checking (a second source, contradictions, newer documents) is a separate verification step the person asks for. Decided with the user on 2026-11-10.

strong.label: the company's own filing or release
strong.rule: an issuer document whose issuer is the subject: its website (a confirmed official domain), its own filings, its own releases (also when carried by a wire service)

strong.label: the other party's own filing or release
strong.rule: for a question about an acquisition, merger or investment: an issuer document by the target, the buyer or the investor named in the question, on its own website or a wire service

strong.label: a regulatory filing
strong.rule: a document on a regulator's own system, whoever filed it (an 8-K by the buyer about the subject counts)
strong.hosts_note: US SEC (EDGAR); India: SEBI, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Reserve Bank of India; Philippines: SEC, Bangko Sentral. Stock exchanges' portals (NSE, BSE, PSE EDGE) are not read: their terms forbid automated use (definitions/skills/statements.json).

strong.label: a Tier 1 news publication
strong.rule: a report by one of these publications
strong.hosts_note: Tier 1 as named by the user (Bloomberg, WSJ, Reuters, etc.). Other major publications (CNBC, Forbes, Fortune, ...) are Tier 2: they need a second independent source.
